details: The International Monetary Fund's latest daily report notes robust US corporate earnings, leading to upward revisions in earnings per share. Inflation markets are currently pricing in minimal risk premium. Despite lingering geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, global equities have maintained weekly gains, while the US dollar is experiencing its second consecutive week of decline. The report also mentioned Banxico cutting rates by 25 bps to 6.5%, signaling an end to their easing cycle, and disappointing German industrial production.
title: IMF Global Markets Monitor Highlights Strong US Earnings and Dollar Decline

details: A recent survey reveals that American crypto investors are increasingly concerned about the future purchasing power of the US dollar. Approximately 49% of respondents have increased their cryptocurrency holdings since January, primarily due to inflation worries. A significant 47% view Bitcoin as a primary store of value, and 73% anticipate cryptocurrencies will play a larger role in the global financial system within the next decade. This sentiment emerged even as Coinbase reported a net loss in Q1, mainly from unrealized declines on crypto investments.
title: US Dollar Concerns Drive American Investors to Increase Crypto Holdings

details: Over the past 24 hours, the cryptocurrency market witnessed total liquidations amounting to $202 million. The majority of these liquidations were from short positions. This occurred amidst a strong performance in traditional US equity markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 reaching new all-time highs following a robust jobs report. This traditional market resilience has generally maintained an elevated risk appetite.
title: Crypto Market Experiences $202 Million in Liquidations
